역시 스바냐량 같은 시대 선지자죠?: He's also a prophet from the same time as Zephaniah, right?
1. 눈물의 예언자 예레미야의 소명: 1. The calling of Jeremiah, the weeping prophet
<렘1:1> 베냐민 땅 아나돗의 제사장 중 힐기야의 아들 예레미야의 말이:
<Jer 1:1> The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin
 - Jeremiah came from a priestly family and was a priest himself. He was called to be a prophet who would deliver God's word.
70세가 넘도록 사역을 했는데 아무도 듣지 않는 설교를 40년 이상 하면:
He ministered until past the age of 70, preaching for more than 40 years to people who didn't listen, and he served with no wife and no children.
 - The only hope in that time was that the people of Israel would come back from Babylon – but only after he himself was dead, so it didn't apply to him. Just like Moses, who had the land of Canaan right in front of him and couldn't go in... And when God calls Jeremiah, he waves it off, saying he's just a child and doesn't know how to speak – that's like Moses too.
 - But God said, 'Don't say you're a child – go,' and He promised that although they'd beat him up, he wouldn't die. Quite a promise, right? You'll get beaten half to death, but you won't die...
2장 입니다. 첫 사랑 - 안 이루어짐. 가슴 시리고 그리운 사랑: Chapter 2. First love - never fulfilled. An aching, longing love
2장은 하나님의 가슴 아픈 첫 사랑 이야기 입니다. 처음 시내산에서 언약: Chapter 2 is the story of God's heartbreaking first love. When He first made the covenant at Mount Sinai, He thought of it like a wedding. Back then God loved Israel so much it was like, 'Just let anybody lay a finger on her – I'll wipe them all out.' God tries in His own way to be patient, struggling as He remembers those good old days, but the people of this time – not one of them even asks, 'Where is that God?'
<렘2:24> 너는 광야에 익숙한 들암나귀가 그 성욕이 동하므로 헐떡거림: <Jer 2:24> A wild ass used to the wilderness, that snuffeth up the wind at her pleasure; in her occasion who can turn her away? all they that seek her will not weary themselves; in her month they shall find her.
I told you, right? Idol worship.
<렘3:11~12> 여호와께서 내게 이르시되 배역한 이스라엘은 패역한 유: <Jer 3:11~12> And the LORD said unto me, The backsliding Israel hath justified herself more than treacherous Judah. 'Backsliding' means turning your back, and 'treacherous' means defying God. He's saying that, the way He feels now, He'd almost be willing to take back backsliding Israel.
<렘5:1> 너희는 예루살렘 거리로 빨리 왕래하며 그 넓은 거리에서 찾아: <Jer 5:1> Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now, and know, and seek in the broad places thereof, if ye can find a man, if there be any that executeth judgment, that seeketh the truth; and I will pardon it.
It's destroyed because there isn't a single righteous person.
<렘7:8~10> 너희가 무익한 거짓말을 의뢰하는도다 너희가 도적질하며:
<Jer 7:8~10> Behold, ye trust in lying words, that cannot profit. Will ye steal, murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense unto Baal, and walk after other gods whom ye know not; and come and stand before me in this house, which is called by my name, and say, We are delivered to do all these abominations?
 - I told you, didn't I? There are people who go to hell with full assurance of salvation. Being a lump of every kind of sin and saying, thank You for saving me – that, He says, is an abomination.
<렘7:16~18> 그런즉 너는 이 백성을 위하여 기도하지 말라 그들을:
<Jer 7:16~18> Therefore pray not thou for this people, neither lift up cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me: for I will not hear thee. Seest thou not what they do in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? The children gather wood, and the fathers kindle the fire, and the women knead their dough, to make cakes to the queen of heaven, and to pour out drink offerings unto other gods, that they may provoke me to anger.
 - The queen of heaven is Ishtar, or Ashtoreth – that's Venus. We talked about it in Genesis. She's a variation of Semiramis. They're serving her. These crazy people.
Since things have come to this, God gives Jeremiah a strange command...
베띠를 하나 가져다가 유브라데 강 바위 틈에 감춰둬라. 여러 날이 지난:
Take a linen belt and hide it in a crack in the rock by the Euphrates River. After many days, He told him to go get it, and when he did, it was completely rotten. 'I'll make you rot good and long beyond the Euphrates (Babylon) for 70 years and then bring you back.' Can you feel God's emotion? You have to feel that.
 - In chapter 14 we see Jeremiah puzzled: God is almighty, so why is He so powerless?
<렘14:9> 어찌하여 놀라 벙벙하는 자 같으시며 구원치 못하는 용사: <Jer 14:9>   Why shouldest thou be as a man astonied, as a mighty man that cannot save?
전능한 무능력자. 이유가 뭐라고 했죠? 자유 때문에. 강제로 할 수 없으: The almighty powerless One. What did we say the reason was? Because of freedom. Because He can't force it. To someone who doesn't get that, He looks like a man stunned and bewildered, you see?
<렘15:2> 그들이 만일 네게 말하기를 우리가 어디로 나아가리요 하거든: <Jer 15:2> And it shall come to pass, if they say unto thee, Whither shall we go forth? then thou shalt tell them, Thus saith the LORD; Such as are for death, to death; and such as are for the sword, to the sword; and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for the captivity, to the captivity.
Why ask me? The ones who are going to die can go ahead and drop dead on their own.
6절 네가 나를 버렸고 내게서 물러갔으므로 네게로 내 손을 펴서 너를 멸: Verse 6: Thou hast forsaken me, saith the LORD, thou art gone backward: therefore will I stretch out my hand against thee, and destroy thee; I am weary with repenting.
일흔 번씩 일곱 번이라도 용서해라. 그건 이론이고...여러분 같은 죄를:
Forgive seventy times seven. That's the theory... How many times do you think you could forgive the same sin?
 - He tells him not to marry, because the children in this land are all going to die and perish.
렘17:2 그들의 자녀가 높은 메 위 푸른 나무 곁에 있는 그 단들과: Jer 17:2  Whilst their children remember their altars and their groves by the green trees upon the high hills.
내 여친이 나 만날 때마다 자꾸 전남친 생각을 하면서 베시시 웃으면 여러: If your girlfriend kept thinking about her ex every time she met you and smiling to herself, how would you feel? If your boyfriend kept staring at photos of his ex and getting lost in old memories, how would you feel? You'd want to sink him in the water, right?
19절 부터는 - 안식일을 좀 지켜라. 진짜 그 놈의 안식일. 쉬는 게:
From verse 19 - please, just keep the Sabbath. Seriously, that Sabbath. Is resting really that hard? Even when He says He'll give you more money?
 - Chapter 18 has the story of the potter. Just as a potter takes clay and makes whatever he wants, He is the One who can do as He pleases with the people of Israel, who are like clay. That's what it says.
그러면서 18절 보시면 예레미야의 말에 귀를 기울이지 말자고 한대요. 그: And then in verse 18 they say, let's not listen to Jeremiah's words. And they even dug a pit to kill Jeremiah.  In the end Jeremiah can't take it anymore and prays a curse. Verses 21~22: Let a cry be heard from their houses, when thou shalt bring a troop suddenly upon them: for they have digged a pit to take me, and hid snares for my feet.
여호와여 그들이 나를 죽이려 하는 계략을 주께서 다 아시오니 그 악을 사: Yet, LORD, thou knowest all their counsel against me to slay me: forgive not their iniquity, neither blot out their sin from thy sight, but let them be overthrown before thee; deal thus with them in the time of thine anger.
살벌하죠? 40년 동안 아무도 안 듣는 설교를 하면서 매일 두둘겨 맞고: Pretty fierce, huh? Imagine preaching for 40 years to people who won't listen, getting beaten up every day, being shunned, and they even dig a pit to kill you. You'd pour out a curse like that too.
19장에는 하나님과 맺은 언약을 안 지키면 모세가 예언했던 데로 자녀의: In chapter 19 He says that if they don't keep the covenant they made with God, the day may come, as Moses prophesied, when they eat the flesh of their own children. So in chapter 20, even after saying, "I'm never prophesying again," he says it's like a fire burning in his heart and he's so frustrated he can't stand it. So he goes and cries out, and gets beaten up again...
급기야 가기 생일을 저주 합니다. 이런 꼬라지 보는 줄 알았으면 안 태어: Finally he curses his own birthday. If I'd known I'd see this mess, it would've been better not to be born.... he says...
21장에 보면 내가 생명의 길과 사망의 길을 두었다 하시는데 생명의 길이:
In chapter 21 He says, I have set before you the way of life and the way of death, and the way of life is surrendering to Babylon. Jeremiah's message is: surrender. A message nobody wants to accept. That's why people turn away from Jeremiah. Because the message isn't pleasant
 - In chapter 22, a king named Jehoiakim builds himself a splendid house of cedar, thinking that if he does, the royal house will gain authority and he'll govern well – and it says that's not how authority is established.
23장에 가면 거짓 선지자들 특히 꿈을 꾸었다고 하는 자들, 이런 놈들의: In chapter 23, the false prophets – especially the ones who say they've had dreams – the goal of these guys is to make the people forget God's name - that's what Satan does.
<렘23:29> 나 여호와가 말하노라 내 말이 불 같지 아니하냐 반석을:
<Jer 23:29>  Is not my word like as a fire? saith the LORD; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?
 - Don't set aside God's word, which is like fire and a hammer, and say you've had a dream.
24장 입니다.\n - 두 무화과 광주리를 보여주시는데 한 광주리는 좋은:
Chapter 24.
 - He shows two baskets of figs: one basket is good figs, and the other basket is figs so rotten they can't be eaten.  And He calls the people being carried off as captives to Babylon the good figs.
In chapter 25 He promises to turn things around when 70 years are complete.
Chapter 26 has the scene where they try to kill Jeremiah but can't.
In chapter 27 it says Jehoiakim, but actually it should be Zedekiah. It went wrong in translation – apart from our Korean Bible, many other Bible versions translate it as Zedekiah.  So, not long after King Zedekiah took the throne, envoys from all the nations came, supposedly to congratulate him on his accession. Right then Jeremiah puts a yoke on his neck, ties it on with cords, and says, "Every nation that doesn't serve the king of Babylon will be wiped out like this."
아니 외국 사절단들도 와 있는데 쪽팔리게 뭐하는거야?: I mean, there are foreign delegations here – what kind of embarrassing stunt is this?
거짓 선지자 하나냐가 예레미야의 멍에를 꺾어버리면서 ‘하나님께서 바벨론의:
The false prophet Hananiah breaks Jeremiah's yoke and lies: 'God has broken the yoke of Babylon. The people taken captive to Babylon will all come back.' He's just running his mouth however he likes.
 - So Jeremiah said amen. Wouldn't it be great if He did that? he says, and as he turns to leave, God says, "Jeremiah, that's a lie. I didn't send him."
 - So Jeremiah prophesied that Hananiah would die, and he died in the seventh month of that year.
 - In chapter 29 Jeremiah sends a letter to Babylon, telling them that they'll be there 70 years, so settle down, live well, and pray for blessing on that nation. Then a man named Shemaiah sends a letter back to Jerusalem saying, what have you been doing, letting him send letters like this – arrest him and kill him right now. God prophesies to Shemaiah: I didn't even send you – why are you acting up? You won't survive.
30장에는 하나님께서 돌이켜 주시기는 하시지만 그래도 무죄한 자로 여기지: Chapter 30 says that God will indeed turn things around, but even so He won't treat them as innocent; He'll correct them justly
31장에는 새로운 언약, 이른바 신약을 세우시는데 남편이 되어도 배반하니:
In chapter 31 He makes a new covenant, the so-called new covenant: since they betray Him even when He's their husband, now God moves from a husband-and-wife relationship to a parent-and-child relationship. It says we enter a covenant where God gives birth to us and we become God's children.
 - Chapter 32 has Him telling Jeremiah to buy the field of Hanameel, the son of his uncle Shallum – proof that even though they're taken captive by Babylon, they'll come back.
 - In the end there is a secret: a righteous Branch will spring up for David and execute justice and righteousness – it prophesies the birth of Christ.
 - In chapter 34 Zedekiah's day of doom approaches. Even so, He says he won't die a miserable death.
35장에 가면 미디안 족속 중 하나인 겐 족속, 그 족속 중 레갑의 아들: Chapter 35 is the story of a man named Jehonadab the son of Rechab, from the Kenites, one of the Midianite clans. God tells Jeremiah, go to the house of the Rechabites and offer them wine. So he does, and the Rechabites say, we won't drink. Why? Verse 6.
우리 선조 요나답이 우리에게 명하여 이르기를 너희와 너희 자손은 영영히: Jonadab the son of Rechab our father commanded us, saying, Ye shall drink no wine, neither ye, nor your sons for ever: neither shall ye build house, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyard, nor have any: but all your days ye shall dwell in tents; that ye may live many days in the land where ye be strangers.
그래서 우리는 그 유언대로 다 지키며 살고 있다. 사실 우리가 여기 와서: So they say, we live keeping all of his last wishes. In fact, the only reason we came here to live is that we had no choice because of Babylon.
14절 보세요. 제가 성경에 하나님의 감탄사가 몇개 안 나온다고 했죠?: Look at verse 14. I told you there are only a few exclamations of God in the Bible, right? Earlier, to Solomon, "You have asked this thing" – that one – and here, "The words of Jonadab the son of Rechab, that he commanded his sons not to drink wine, are performed!!"
왜 감탄사가 터졌어요?: Why did He burst out with an exclamation?
그들은 그 선조의 명령을 순종하여 오늘까지 마시지 아니하거늘 내가 너희에: For unto this day they drink none, but obey their father's commandment: notwithstanding I have spoken unto you, rising early and speaking; but ye hearkened not unto me!!
<렘35:18~19> 예레미야가 레갑 족속에게 이르되 만군의 여호와 이스: <Jer 35:18~19> And Jeremiah said unto the house of the Rechabites, Thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Because ye have obeyed the commandment of Jonadab your father, and kept all his precepts, and done according unto all that he hath commanded you: therefore thus saith the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel; Jonadab the son of Rechab shall not want a man to stand before me for ever.
- 이 사람들이 지금도 그런 원시적인 삶을 산다. 예수님을 믿지도 않고: - These people still live that primitive kind of life today. They don't believe in Jesus and their doctrine isn't complete, but because of their faithfulness and integrity, He says, they shall not want a man to stand before Me forever. I told you, right? We're saved by faith, but that word is more often translated faithfulness or loyalty. Then if you say we're saved by being faithful, it becomes a completely different story.
하나님께서 요시야 때부터 지금까지 내가 했던 말들을 다 기록해라. 혹시:
God says, write down everything I've said from the days of Josiah until now. If perhaps they hear and turn back, I'll forgive them.   So Baruch writes it down.  When it's all written down, Jeremiah tells Baruch to go to the temple and read it to the people. God's wrath is now filled to the brim.
 - In the fifth year of Jehoiakim, he's first called before the officials and reads it to them.  They're shocked: we'll report this to the king. You go and hide well, you and Jeremiah.  And so it's read....
<렘36:23> 여후디가 삼 편 사 편을 낭독하면 왕이 소도로 그것을 연:
<Jer 36:23> And it came to pass, that when Jehudi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed in the fire that was on the hearth.
 - King Jehoiakim burns Jeremiah's scroll. He's the ancestor of people who burn Bibles. So God tells him to write the book again, and because of this, the book of Jeremiah looks a bit jumbled. There was so much content that rewriting it must have been hard. Baruch would write for a while and then put in the parts he'd left out here and there, and that's how it ended up that way. The original book of Jeremiah was burned by Jehoiakim.
 - Chapter 37: when news came that the Chaldean soldiers had withdrawn after hearing a rumor that Egypt had come up, the hearts of the people of Judah leaned toward Egypt again
그러니가 예레미야가 오히려 애굽의 군대가 다시 돌아가고 갈대아 인들은 돌:
So Jeremiah says instead that the Egyptian army will go back home, and the Chaldeans won't leave. Even if only the wounded among the Chaldean soldiers were left, they would set Jerusalem on fire and tear it down.
 - Remember how last time he sent a letter to Babylon, and a false prophet there sent a letter back saying to arrest Jeremiah right away and kill him? So the riffraff went in a mob to King Zedekiah saying Jeremiah has to be killed. And King Zedekiah just handed him over.  So those people threw Jeremiah into a pit. Luckily it was a mud pit, so he survived.
 - Then Ebedmelech, a Cushite (Ethiopian) eunuch, says this is wrong and tells them to pull Jeremiah out. The one person with any sense – and it's only Ebedmelech the Cushite.
 - Then Zedekiah asks Jeremiah, whom they pulled out like that, whether Babylon is coming again.
It's coming, he says. The false prophets: it's not coming.
그런데 안 오긴 뭘 안와. B.C 606년에 여호야김 3년에 느부갓네살:
But not coming? Of course it came.  In B.C 606, in the third year of Jehoiakim, Nebuchadnezzar came and carried off people like Daniel, Mishael, Hananiah, and Azariah in the first deportation.
 - You'd think the false prophets would have nothing to say even if they had ten mouths, but the false prophets lie again. It came once by chance, but it won't come again. Why? Because it already came and went. But Jeremiah says it's coming again.
온다 안온다 온다 안온다 싸우는데 B.C 597년에 또 다시 와서 여호야: It's coming, it's not coming, it's coming, it's not coming – they argue, and in B.C 597 it came again, captured King Jehoiakim, carried off Ezekiel too, and so on.
두번이나 속았으면...또 온다. 대항하지 말고 사로잡혀 가면 생명을 노략:
If you've been fooled twice... It's coming again. Don't resist; if you go into captivity, you'll gain your life like plunder, he says.
 - Even though Jeremiah pleaded that earnestly, Zedekiah is worried about being embarrassed in front of the people who were taken captive before him.
 - Finally, Nebuchadnezzar comes a third time, and on the 10th day of the 10th month of King Zedekiah's 9th year (BC 588)  he besieges the city for a year and a half.  He surrounds it for a year and a half, until the 9th day of the 4th month of B.C 586, so countless people starve to death, and the king flees as far as the plains of Jericho, but the Babylonian army chases him, catches him, and drags him to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
시드기야 앞에서 왕자들을 다 죽이고, 대신들을 다 죽이고 시드기야의 눈을:
Chapter 39 is the miserable scene where they kill all the princes in front of Zedekiah, kill all the officials, gouge out Zedekiah's eyes, and drag him all the way to Babylon
 - After that, from the 7th day of the 5th month the temple in Jerusalem starts to burn, and by the 10th day of the 5th month all of Jerusalem is burned up.  At this time they take Jeremiah too, but they let him go on the way. Jeremiah goes back to Jerusalem.
 - At this time Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam and grandson of Shaphan, became governor over the people who were left, and he tells them to serve Babylon faithfully. So a man named Ishmael plotted to kill Gedaliah. Someone told him about it, but he didn't believe it.
- In the end Gedaliah is assassinated in chapter 41, and this is in the 7th month. And so these become the four great fast days
10월의 금식은 10월 10일 예루살렘이 최종적으로 포위당했던 것: The fast of the 10th month is for the 10th day of the 10th month, when Jerusalem was finally besieged
4월의 금식은 4월 9일 성이 함락된 것: The fast of the 4th month is for the 9th day of the 4th month, when the city fell
5월의 금식은 5월 7일부터 10일까지 예루살렘 성전과 왕궁이 불타버린: The fast of the 5th month is for the 7th to the 10th day of the 5th month, when the temple and royal palace in Jerusalem burned down
7월의 금식은 총독 그다랴가 암살당한 것: The fast of the 7th month is for the assassination of Governor Gedaliah
잘 기억해 두세요. 이거 에스겔 할 때 또 나오니까.\n - 그리고 42:
Remember these well. They come up again when we do Ezekiel.
 - And in chapter 42, since they killed the governor and it looks like Babylon will invade again, they ask Jeremiah again: is Babylon coming? And Jeremiah says it won't come again, so settle down and make your home in this land. And then in chapter 43, they stubbornly insist: it's going to come again, and you say it won't?
바벨론이 오지도 않는데 애굽으로 도망가면서 또 예레미야도 끌고 간다. 다: Babylon isn't even coming, but they flee to Egypt and drag Jeremiah along too. When they arrive at the square in Tahpanhes, Jeremiah digs a big pit, buries large stones in it, and warns the people of Israel.
바벨론 왕 느부갓네살이 그 보좌를 내가 감추게 한 이 돌 위에 두고 애굽: Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon will set his throne upon these stones that I have hid, and he shall smite the land of Egypt, and deliver such as are for death to death; and such as are for captivity to captivity; and such as are for the sword to the sword
이것이 예루살렘을 향한 예레미야의 마지막 말. 그리고 애가서를 쓴 것 같:
These are Jeremiah's last words toward Jerusalem. And then it seems he wrote Lamentations.
 - In chapter 44, the people of Israel who still wouldn't listen.
 - Chapter 45 is a personal word to Baruch – I'll keep you alive.
